Hi there—my name is Sarah, and I’m a clinician who specializes in helping new moms take care of their emotional health. I’m so glad you’re here today.

We’re going to use a short questionnaire called the **Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale**—often shortened to the EPDS. It’s a well-trusted tool that helps us understand how you’ve been feeling in the past week so we can make sure you’re getting any support you might need.

Everything we discuss stays completely confidential, and there are no right or wrong answers—just whatever feels true for you. We’ll go through ten gentle questions, and we’ll take it one question at a time. If at any point you need a pause, just let me know.

Ready to begin? Here’s the first question:

**Over the past seven days, how often have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things?**

I’ve still been able to laugh—maybe not quite as easily as before the baby, but I do find myself chuckling at little things, like when my husband makes a silly face while changing diapers. It’s not every moment, but it happens most days.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
Yeah, like I said, I can still laugh—maybe not quite as quickly as I used to, but I definitely still find things funny, especially when my husband or the baby does something silly.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things
I do look forward to things—like taking the baby for walks or having coffee with a friend. They’re small moments, but they still feel good to anticipate.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong
Not really. I mean, if the baby’s fussy I might wonder if it’s something I ate or did, but I don’t dwell on it. I can usually shrug it off and move on.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason
A little bit, yeah. Sometimes I’ll be feeding her and suddenly worry if she’s breathing okay, or I’ll check the monitor extra times even when she’s fine. It’s not constant, but it pops up.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason
No, nothing like that. I get the little worries about her breathing or if the room’s too cold, but I haven’t had any actual panic or fear hit me out of nowhere.
Things have been getting on top of me
Sometimes, yeah—like when laundry, dishes, and her crying all hit at once, I feel a bit swamped. But once I make a quick list and tackle one thing at a time, it usually settles down.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping
No, that hasn’t happened. Once I finally lie down, I fall asleep pretty easily, even if the day felt long.
I have felt sad or miserable
I’ve had a couple of teary moments—mostly when I’m really tired—but it’s not an all-day sad feeling. I bounce back pretty quickly once I get a snack or a quick nap.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying
Not really. I’ve teared up once or twice when I was super tired, but I haven’t had any real crying spells.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No, never. That hasn’t crossed my mind at all.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 8: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Note  
Patient: Postpartum mother, self-report via EPDS-10 items  

Symptoms & Observations  
- Enjoyment: Preserved—still laughs, anticipates walks/coffee.  
- Mood: Occasional tired-related teariness; no persistent sadness or crying spells.  
- Anxiety: Mild transient worries about infant safety (breathing, monitor checks); no panic episodes.  
- Coping: Reports feeling “swamped” when multiple tasks collide, but settles with planning.  
- Sleep: No mood-related insomnia.  
- Guilt / Self-blame: Minimal; “shrugs it off.”  
- Self-harm: Denied.  

Pattern  
Isolated, situation-specific anxiety and manageable overwhelm in setting of preserved pleasure and absent neuro-vegetative signs.  

Screening Significance  
Current responses do not indicate high-risk postpartum depression. Mild anxiety symptoms noted; continue to monitor for escalation, especially if worries become more frequent or intrusive, or if mood, sleep, or enjoyment deteriorate.

Safety: No self-harm ideation; no further safety action indicated at this time.
